extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their attorneys/agents seeking USPTO Track One prioritized examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing a Request for Prioritized Examination (Track One) with the USPTO, covering eligibility, required documents and fees, timing rules, procedural consequences (dismissal/refund), and filing formats for new applications and RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal / target disposition time
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's goal for prioritized examination is to provide a final disposition within twelve months, on average, of the date that prioritized status was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program objective (final disposition within 12 months). It is a target/goal rather than an absolute guarantee, and describes expected expedited processing timelines under Track One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required upon filing (new application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees required to be paid upon filing for Prioritized Examination (Track One) for a new application include: i. Basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a) or 1.16(c) for plant); ii. Search fee (37 CFR 1.16(k) or 1.16(m) for plant); iii. Examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(o) or 1.16(q) for plant); iv. Publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) — currently set to $0 but still required by rule; v. Track One processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)(1)); vi. Track One prioritized examination fee ($4,200.00; $1,680 for small entities; $840 for micro entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the above fees are unpaid at filing, the Request for Prioritized Examination will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge the missing fees is provided in the papers accompanying the application and the request (in which case the fees will be charged per the authorization and the request will not be dismissed). It is recommended to include an authorization to charge any additional fees under 37 CFR §§ 1.16 and 1.17 to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required upon filing (RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests for prioritized examination filed in connection with a request for continued examination (RCE), the required fees (if not previously paid) include: i. Applicable publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) — currently $0; ii. Prioritized examination processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)(1)); iii. Prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)) ($4,200; $1,680 small; $840 micro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any fee is unpaid at the time of filing the request for prioritized examination with an RCE, the request will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge additional required fees is provided in the papers accompanying the request. The Track One processing fee will be retained if the request is dismissed; only the Track One prioritized examination fee is refundable automatically on dismissal (see refund rules). Consult the current fee schedule for exact amounts and any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of nonpayment and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: If required fees are unpaid at filing, the Request for Prioritized Examination will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge missing fees is present in the accompanying papers. Upon dismissal, only the Track One prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)) will be refunded automatically; the Track One processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) will be retained to cover processing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other application fees (basic filing, search, examination, application size/excess claim fees) cannot be refunded per 37 CFR 1.26, though a petition for express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(d)) may permit refund of search/excess claim fees. Publication fee refund may be requested per MPEP 1126 if the application is not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b). Include authorizations to charge fees to avoid dismissal, and note retained vs refundable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic application formal-content requirements on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper Request for Prioritized Examination requires that the application include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including claim(s) and any required drawings, and either an executed inventor's oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.64 for each inventor, or a signed ADS providing each inventor's legal name, mailing address, and residence (if not residing at the mailing address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit these required items on the date of filing will cause the request to be dismissed. If an ADS with the required inventor information is present on filing, the inventor's oath or declaration need not be submitted on filing. For guidance on inventor's oaths/declarations and substitute statements, see referenced USPTO examples and 37 CFR provisions. Applications must be in condition for examination (see MPEP 708.02 VIII.C) before a request will be acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-count and claim-type limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An application seeking prioritized examination may contain no more than 4 independent claims, no more than 30 total claims, and no multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant mistakenly fails to comply with these claim-count/type requirements, the applicant will receive a decision on the Request for Prioritized Examination that provides one month to take corrective action; that one-month period is not extendable. Excess claims fees or application size fees are not required to be present on filing but should be paid to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by application type and filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Original nonprovisional utility and plant patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), filed on or after September 26, 2011, are eligible for prioritized examination (Track One), provided they meet claim limits and other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, original nonprovisional utility and plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, or having entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, in which a proper RCE has been filed or is concurrently being filed, are eligible for prioritized examination under the RCE pathway (subject to RCE-specific timing and conditions). The effective date of Track One for new applications is September 26, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE-specific eligibility and timing (prosecution closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application with a request for continued examination (RCE) to be eligible for prioritized examination, a proper RCE can only be filed if prosecution in the application is closed (e.g., the last Office action is a final action, a notice of allowance, or an action that otherwise closes prosecution per 37 CFR 1.114(b)). A Request for Prioritized Examination must be made before an Office action responsive to the RCE has been mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Request for Prioritized Examination must be filed prior to the mailing of a first Office action after the filing of the RCE, and may be filed concurrently with or subsequent to the RCE filing (but before the responsive Office action). For national-stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, prioritized examination of the national-stage application itself is not available; however, upon filing a proper RCE (when prosecution is closed), prioritized examination becomes available for such national-stage entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and medium for filing Requests (utility vs plant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Prioritized Examination of utility patent applications must be filed using EFS-Web. Requests for Prioritized Examination of plant patent applications must be filed in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow USPTO filing-system requirements for the application type. For continuations or other special filings, ensure you use the correct medium to avoid processing delays or dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statements, inventor declarations, and continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the inventor's oath or declaration from a parent application may be submitted for a continuing application, provided the earlier-filed oath/declaration is compliant with current rules (37 CFR 1.63(d)). If a joint inventor has refused to execute an oath/declaration, a substitute statement and the declaration(s) from the other joint inventor(s), or a signed ADS with each inventor's legal name, mailing address, and residence, must be submitted on the date the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the signed ADS is not present on filing, or the substitute statement is defective for any reason, prioritized examination status will not be granted. See USPTO examples and 'Inventor's Oath or Declaration Examples' for best practices when submitting substitute statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of pre-examination notices and informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-examination notice identifying missing items or informalities will delay a decision on a pending Request for Prioritized Examination until after applicant files a complete and timely reply; such notices do not automatically cause dismissal (unless required items are missing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for prioritized examination are acted upon once the application meets all formal requirements such that it is ready for examination (MPEP 708.02 VIII.C). Informalities like noncompliant paper formatting, language issues, or excess claims notices may delay the decision but not necessarily dismiss the request; however, missing required items (specification, claims, required fees, oath/declaration or ADS) on the filing date will cause dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) and prioritized status
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an IDS in an application that includes a Request for Prioritized Examination will not result in dismissal of a pending request, nor will it terminate special status if granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS filings do not by themselves affect prioritized status; applicants should still ensure IDSs are filed in compliance with IDS rules to avoid other prosecution issues or delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension of time, including an extension to respond to a pre-examination notice (e.g., Notice to File Missing Parts), will cause the application to be ineligible for further treatment under the prioritized examination (Track One) program. A request for an extension of time prior to the grant of prioritized examination status will prevent such status from being granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file extension requests if you intend to obtain or retain Track One status; timely responses without extensions are required to remain in the program. An extension request after grant may cause loss of further prioritized treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-request limits per application/RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The prioritized examination program permits only a single request to be granted associated with a request for continued examination under 37 C.F.R. 1.114 in that application. Separately, the program permits a single request to be granted upon filing a new application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), and a single request to be granted upon filing a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot obtain multiple Track One grants for the same application/RCE pairing; plan use of the single available Track One request accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication requests and publication fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You may file an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) with a nonpublication request together with a Request for Prioritized Examination (Track One). Although the publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) is required by rule, it is currently set to $0 so no fee is due at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publication fee is changed in the future to a non-zero amount, that fee amount must be submitted with the Request for Prioritized Examination even if a nonpublication request is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and contacts for dismissed decisions or questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant receives a decision dismissing a Request for Prioritized Examination, the applicant can file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 if they believe the dismissal was not proper. Contact information for questions: the person who signed the dismissal decision, the Office of Petitions (571-272-3282), or the Office of Patent Legal Administration (571-272-7704 or PatentPractice@uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the reasons stated in a dismissal decision and determine whether an error was made by the USPTO before filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.181. For refund questions and other procedural matters, use the listed contacts; for fee schedules consult the USPTO fee pages.
